summary: Lucjan Malinowski was a linguist who studied at Uniwersytet Petersburski, Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Jena, and Jagiellonian University. He served as professor of Slavic philology at Jagiellonian University from circa 1877 to 1898.
Lucy Annette Jones specialized in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University, where she studied under doctoral supervisors Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.
Lucy Bulliet was an Indologist who studied at Pomona College and earned her PhD at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She later taught Vedic Religion at Columbia University.

Indologist and linguist Ludo Rocher studied at Ghent, Utrecht, and SOAS under Adriaan Scharpé and Jan Gonda. He taught at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and was a professor and chair at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2004).

Ludvig Frands Adalbert Wimmer was a linguist who earned his MA and PhD at the University of Copenhagen, studying under Niels Ludvig Westergaard. He spent his career at Copenhagen, becoming Professor of Nordic Philology (1886–1910).

Indologist Ludwig Alsdorf studied under Walther Schubring at Hamburg and Heinrich Lüders at Berlin. He taught at Allahabad, Münster, and Berlin before holding the chair for Indian history and culture at the University of Hamburg from 1950 to 1978.

Ludwig Bachhofer worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Sinology. After completing his PhD at the University of Munich under Lucian Scherman, he was a Privatdozent there (1927–1935) and Assistant Professor of Art at the University of Chicago (1935–1965).

Ludwig Diestel was a religious studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the universities of Bonn (circa 1858–1862), Greifswald (circa 1862–1867), Jena (circa 1867–1872), and Tübingen (circa 1872–1879).

Ludwig Fritze was an Indologist who studied at Lehrerseminar Oranienburg (~1851–1854). He served as a teacher at teacher seminars in Oranienburg (1861–1871), Zabern (1871–1873), and Drossen (1873–1885), and as Oberlehrer at Köpenick (1885–1906).

Ludwig Heinrich Kapff worked in Indology and religious studies, earning his PhD at the University of Tübingen (1826–1829). He was a Privatdozent at Tübingen (1830–1833), Rector in Heilbronn, and Ephorus at Seminare Maulbronn und Blaubeuren (1854–1869).

Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn at Göttingen (Dr. phil. 1894). He worked at the Royal Library of Berlin and spent his main academic career at the University of Greifswald (1897–1920+).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar of linguistics and classical archaeology who studied at Leipzig and Göttingen. He held professorships at Charles University (1853–1859), the University of Giessen (from 1859), and the University of Leipzig (from 1871).

Ludwig Oster was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Richard Pischel and completed his PhD at Heidelberg University under Christian Bartholomae and Salomon Lefmann.

Ludwig Poley was an Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin and Eugène Burnouf and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Padua (1866) and the University of Vienna (1867).

Ludwig Ross was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Kiel University. He held academic posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).

Linguist Ludwig Sütterlin studied at Leipzig and Heidelberg, earning his PhD under Hermann Osthoff. He served as Privatdozent and associate professor at Heidelberg (1890–1913) and held the chair of comparative linguistics at Freiburg (1913–1924).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Technische Hochschule Berlin, Manchester, and the University of Cambridge, earning his PhD at Cambridge in 1929. He was a fellow at Trinity College and served as philosophy professor at Cambridge (1930–1947).

Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied at Lviv, EPHE, and Collège de France under scholars including Stefan Stasiak, Louis Renou, and Jules Bloch. He served as professor at the University of Breslau from 1945 to 1978.

Indologist Ludwik Sternbach earned law and doctoral degrees at Jagiellonian University and Lviv under Helena Willman-Grabowska and Stefan Stasiak. He held posts at Lviv, Mumbai, Sorbonne Nouvelle (1970–1972), and Collège de France (1972–1976).

Luigi Heilmann was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Padua and Bologna under Luigi Suali and Ambrogio Ballini. He held posts at Sacred Heart, Cagliari, and Pavia, later serving as professor of linguistics at Bologna (~1963–1981).
